emma: Quick note — ran into import confusion in our JS SDK docs. We show both `require` and `import` but not which runtime each targets.
emma: Repro: CJS lambda using `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` then `new Redwood()` -> TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor.
luke: That usually means the package exported default in ESM so the CJS consumer sees `{ default: [Function] }`.
yvonne: For the docs, can we add a tiny matrix: CJS (require named), CJS (require .default), ESM (named), ESM (default), and a short TS note about `esModuleInterop`?
emma: Also include a one-line Edge note: "Edge runtimes are ESM-only — prefer named imports."
luke: Good call. Add troubleshooting: `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/inference')"` and common errors mapping.
docs-bot: Created issue SDK-DOCS-247: add import parity guide and quickstart blurb (PR requested).
yvonne: I'll draft the PR with examples for Next.js edge, Cloudflare Worker, Node CJS, and TS config snippet.
emma: Thanks — hopefully this cuts down on the support tickets.
